title: 2 Samuel 20
paragraphs: ¹ Now a troublemaker happened to be there, a man named Sheba son of Bicri, a Benjaminite. He blew a trumpet and shouted, "We have no share in David, no part in Jesse's son! Every man to his tent, Israel!" ² So all the men of Israel deserted David and followed Sheba son of Bicri. But the men of Judah stayed loyal to their king, all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. ³ When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to take care of the palace and put them under guard. He provided for them but had no relations with them. They were kept in seclusion until the day they died, living as if in widowhood. ⁴ The king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah for me within three days, and be here yourself." ⁵ So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time the king had set.

⁶ David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bicri will do us more harm now than Absalom ever did. Take your lord's men and pursue him, or he'll find fortified cities and slip away from us." ⁷ So Joab's men, the Cherethites and Pelethites, and all the mighty warriors marched out of Jerusalem after Sheba son of Bicri. ⁸ When they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his battle dress, and he had a dagger strapped to his belt at his hip. As he stepped forward, it slipped out. ⁹ Joab said to Amasa, "How are you, my brother?" And Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him. ¹⁰ Amasa was not watching the dagger in Joab's other hand, and Joab drove it into his belly, spilling out his intestines on the ground. He did not need to stab him again, and Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai continued in pursuit of Sheba son of Bicri.

¹¹ One of Joab's men stood over Amasa and called out, "Anyone who favors Joab and is for David, follow Joab!" ¹² Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. The man saw that everyone was stopping there, so he dragged Amasa off the road into a field and threw a garment over him, since anyone who came by stopped to look. ¹³ Once Amasa was moved from the road, all the men followed Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bicri. ¹⁴ Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel Beth Maakah, and all the Bicrites gathered together and followed him. ¹⁵ All Joab's troops came and besieged Sheba at Abel Beth Maakah. They built a siege ramp against the city, and it stood against the outer wall while all Joab's troops battered the wall to bring it down.

¹⁶ Then a wise woman called from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I can speak to him." ¹⁷ When he came near, the woman asked, "Are you Joab?" "I am," he answered. "Then listen to what your servant has to say," she said. "I'm listening," he replied. ¹⁸ She continued, "Long ago people used to say, 'Get your answer at Abel,' and that settled matters. ¹⁹ I am one of the peaceable and faithful in Israel. You are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you want to swallow up the LORD's inheritance?" ²⁰ Joab replied, "Far be it from me, far be it indeed, to swallow up or destroy!

²¹ That is not my aim. There is a man named Sheba son of Bicri, from the hill country of Ephraim, who has raised his hand against King David. Hand him over alone, and I'll withdraw from the city." "His head will be thrown to you over the wall," the woman replied. ²² Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bicri and threw it to Joab. He sounded the trumpet, and his troops withdrew from the city, each to his home. And Joab returned to the king at Jerusalem. ²³ Now Joab was in command of all Israel's army; Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the Cherethites and Pelethites; ²⁴ Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the historian; ²⁵ Sheva was the secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were the priests;
²⁶ And Ira the Jairite was also David's personal priest.
